newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen's Islah party walks out in budget protest.
newsitem.headline: Yemen's Islah party walks out in budget protest.

text.p: The junior partner in Yemen's coalition government on Monday walked out of a parliamentary session in protest against the 1997 budget, parliamentary sources said.
The Islamist Islah Party withdrew after a special budget committee, which includes Islah members, presented its final report to the assembly and called for a vote.
"The budget should have been discussed in detail before the approval of the cabinet and its discussion in parliament," an Islah source told Reuters.
But a parliamentary source said the Islah members had walked out in protest against proposals to merge the budget of religious institutes with the budget of the education ministry.

Islah, headed by parliament speaker Sheikh Abdullah al-Ahmar, controls the institutes where a religious curriculum is followed. It allocates a special budget for these schools. President Ali Abdullah Saleh has called on the government to close down the religious institutes and unify the two curricula.
On December 5, Yemen's cabinet approved the 1997 national budget, with spending estimated at 313 billion rials ($3.13 billion) and revenues forecast at 301 billion rials.
The Islah members had also walked out of the cabinet session and were not present when the cabinet approved the budget.
The budget must be endorsed by parliament and the president must then give final approval.
Islah controls about 22 percent of seats in parliament while Saleh's General Peoples Congress holds about 50 percent. ($1=100 rials)
